original_card.question: Can one specified masked or overcomplete decoder improve the complete moment budget?
methods: Synthesize a decoder with exact coefficients and fully priced helper endpoints.
Bound the best possible budget for a fixed support alphabet before synthesis.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Change an assumption of the eight-term all-pairs bound and count all copied information, frames and restoration.

first_step.inspect: Locate the excluded classes: masked identities, at least nine terms, and deeper punctures.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Choose one finite support alphabet and test exact decoding constraints before building a whole network.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A cheaper fully realized decoder could increase deficit or lower recursive cost on the binding complex side.
allowed_variations: Select a specific masked or overcomplete family with exact labels and supports.
scope_change_triggers: Repeating the exact eight-term all-pairs search inside its proved scope.

scope_change_reason: The assigned structural-decoder track was narrowed to one seed-selected P120 root pencil, one forced-rational row family, and the existing C.6 shared-extra-total assembly rule.
actual_scope: For P120, e=L_51 and d0=L_1, exhaust all 120 targets and all 511 nonzero nine-bit sink labels in the calibrated one-row ansatz, then all distinct-target pairs with one shared required-source total. The result is a finite negative result for that family only.
bottleneck_link: A two-target shared total must be available at both relaxed sinks and preserve a nonzero diagonal at each target; this audit finds every available pair contaminates both diagonals.
stop_rule: Enumerate every eligible target/sink-label row and every distinct-target pair after the forced-mu and nonzero-diagonal filters; stop when the finite domain is exhausted.
evidence: The exact replay reconstructs 27 P120 row nodes from 61,320 target/sink trials; all 351 distinct-target pairs admit the union total at both sinks, but each contaminates both target diagonals, leaving zero exact pairs. A P112 known-witness positive control and two certificate-mutation controls also pass.
author: Cinna Davis
ai_assistance: Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance with search design, exact replay implementation, proof explanation, and packaging; the assignment seed and research direction were user-directed.

open_questions.question: Can an exact P120 pair exist when a row has no off-target calibrating source and its rational mu is selected by a different complete argument?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This search excludes rows whose forced rational parameter cannot be inferred from a nonzero e-pairing, so closing that case would enlarge the audited family.
open_questions.first_step: For one no-calibrator row, derive all mu values allowed by its diagonal and off-target zero conditions before enumerating pairs.
open_questions.blocked_by: The current task fixes the calibrated C.6 row family; no-calibrator rows require a separate complete parameter argument.
